gloss: to give one's all; to spare no effort
teaser: Today, we explore the power of giving it your all.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore the power of giving it your all. [break 1s] The phrase is: 全力以赴, quán lì yǐ fù. [break 1s] 全 (quán) - all; [break 0.5s] 力 (lì) - strength; [break 0.5s] 以 (yǐ) - to use; [break 0.5s] 赴 (fù) - to go to or to commit. [break 1s] The full idiom again: 全力以赴 literally means 'to use all strength to commit,' and figuratively, it means 'to give one's all.' [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a historical context where armies would commit all their resources and strength to a battle, leaving no room for retreat. It emphasizes a mindset of total dedication and effort, no matter the challenges ahead. Over time, it has been adopted in various contexts, including personal goals and teamwork. [break 1.5s] Example one: 我们必须全力以赴才能赢得比赛。 [break 1s] We must give our all to win the game. [break 1s] Example two: 在这个项目中，他全力以赴，结果非常成功。 [break 1s] He gave his all in this project, and the results were very successful. [break 1s] Example three: 如果想通过考试，学生们应该全力以赴。 [break 1s] If they want to pass the exam, students should give their all. [break 1s] So, remember: 全力以赴 means to give one's all. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
